title: IBRNet: Learning Multi-View Image-Based Rendering
layout_note: Three columns: a 3-D scene column (source and target photos around a dotted scene cube with one orange ray), a beige middle panel (per-sample MLPs feeding a ray transformer, with a rounded detail callout of one MLP at its bottom), and a right column of volume-rendering plot over the rendering loss, joined by hollow block arrows.
grouping: The learned part sits on one pale beige rounded background panel; a darker beige rounded callout inside it, attached by a wedge to one of the three MLP glyphs, zooms into that MLP. Views are told apart by frame style keyed in a top-left legend: solid green frames for source views, dotted dark-red frame for the target view. Bold titles head the right column steps.
shapes_depth: Source and target views are photo cards tilted in perspective around a dotted wireframe box holding the object render; the target ray is a thick orange arrow from a small camera-eye glyph, with three blue sample dots; dashed lavender and cyan lines project a sample into source views A and B. MLPs are three thin unfilled rectangles; the ray transformer is a large rounded square with faint all-to-all lines inside. Inputs in the callout are hatched striped bars whose stripe colours are keyed in a mini legend (image colour, viewing direction, image feature). The density plot reuses the orange ray as its x-axis with the three blue dots on it; the loss is two colour squares inside norm bars.
proposed_highlight: The learned modules are grouped on the single tinted panel and the new cross-sample module is the largest box there, drawn with faint internal connections; the zoom callout expands one per-sample MLP in place.
lesson: Reuse the scene ray as the density plot's x-axis, with the same coloured sample dots placed on it, so the volume-rendering step visibly comes from the ray drawn in the scene.
notes: venue CVPR from Semantic Scholar (venue_source: semantic-scholar); year = arXiv preprint year (2102.13090), the same as the CVPR year. Photos of the scene are embedded rasters.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

core.what: an orange target ray pierces a dotted cube around the real scene, and its blue sample points send dashed coloured lines into the green-framed source photos A and B, before feeding a row of per-sample MLPs

relations.form: left zone: real toy photos as source views (green frames A, B) and the target view (red dotted frame) around a wire cube; three blue dots on the orange ray, with dashed purple and cyan projection lines to views A and B

three straight horizontal arrows from the sample points to three MLP glyphs in a beige tinted zone, outputs c_i and f_σ,i, then into a rounded 'Ray Transformer', out as σ1-σ3; hollow block arrows lead on to Volume Rendering and down to Rendering Loss
inside the Ray Transformer thin criss-crossing lines join every sample's f_σ,i to every σ output

a beige wedge from the middle MLP opens a rounded inset where views A and B each supply a hatched feature bar (image colour / viewing direction / image feature, keyed) into one MLP giving 'color c' and 'density feature f_σ'
the loss is drawn as two coloured squares color_pred minus color_gt inside a squared norm, below a density-vs-ray-distance plot whose blue dots match the sample points

channels.colour: frame colour = view role (green solid source, red dotted target, keyed); orange = the target ray and its distance axis; blue dots = ray samples; purple/cyan dashes = source view A/B, reused as the outline of each view's feature bar; hatch colours = feature type (keyed), with purple meaning both 'view A' and 'viewing direction'
channels.shape: photos = views, three-bar glyphs = MLPs, rounded box = Ray Transformer, hatched bars = per-view features, coloured squares = pixel colours
channels.line: solid black = data flow, dashed coloured = projection to a source view, hollow arrows = stage transitions, thin violet lines = attention inside the transformer
channels.frame: beige tinted zone = the network; rounded inset = MLP detail; green/red frames = source/target views

quality.strengths: The geometry the method relies on (a target ray, its samples, their projections into source photos) is drawn on real images, and the samples keep their blue dots from the scene through to the density plot; the per-view features are drawn as keyed bars in the inset; the loss compares drawn colour patches, not a formula.
quality.weaknesses: Purple means both source view A and the viewing-direction hatch; the Ray Transformer's interior is a tangle of faint lines that conveys 'all-to-all' only vaguely; the output side (volume rendering, loss) switches to hollow block arrows and a separate column, so the flow bends down at the right.

insights.structure: Three zones left to right: a scene zone with real source photos (green frames A, B) and a red-dotted target view around a wire cube pierced by an orange ray, a beige tinted network zone with per-sample MLPs feeding a rounded 'Ray Transformer', and a right column with a volume-rendering density plot above a rendering-loss equation.
insights.data: Inputs are real toy photographs; sample points on the ray are blue dots whose projections into source views are dashed coloured lines; per-view features are hatched striped bars keyed as image color / viewing direction / image feature.
insights.emphasis: A callout wedge from the MLP stack opens a rounded inset showing how views A and B feed one MLP, and the loss is shown with actual coloured squares color_pred - color_gt inside a norm.
insights.flow: Left to right along horizontal arrows from ray samples to MLPs to Ray Transformer to sigma outputs, then a hollow block arrow right to the density plot and a hollow arrow down to the loss.
insights.avoid: The colour-coded hatched feature swatches are small and need the inset key to decode; the scene zone has no frame so it is grouped only by proximity.

arrangement.units: unframed scene area on the left, a beige tinted network panel in the middle with a rounded zoom inset, and an unframed output column on the right
arrangement.inputs_as: real photographs of the scene as tilted source/target view cards
arrangement.losses_at: bottom-right, rendering loss equation with colour swatches
arrangement.shared: one MLP applied to each ray sample (three identical stacks)
